text:
zoe: fyi, after the predictive-batching merge we're seeing KV cache fragmentation spike and a handful of longctx OOMs on canary nodes
zoe: repros show large free-list holes, mem usage steady but allocable drops rapidly
matt: on it, link to the PR?
zoe: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2857 : the change adjusts batch boundary packing heuristics to favor filling payloads
ashley: we've got alerts: `kv_free_ratio` went from 0.73 -> 0.92 on canary-3 over ~15min :scream: 
ci-bot: Perf test `longctx-memory-smoke` failed on canary-3 (seq=4096) — job 7234
sre-ops: holding rollout to next gate, marking rollout:blocked :no_entry_sign:
nora: logs pasted: ```OOM killer invoked: pid=8421 comm=runner_alloc
Killed process 8421 (runtime-worker) total-vm:125G rss:102G anon-rss:100G```
devx: quick repro command if you want to reproduce locally: `./tools/run_inference --model rwd-longctx --seq-len 4096 --batching predictive --warmup 100`
kai: profile snapshot attached in internal perf (link) shows hot path in `slab_alloc` and unusual scatter in `free_list_walk`
james: could be batch boundary alignment causing small tail allocations to fragment slabs instead of coalescing
zoe: i ran a trace: `kv_frag_ratio=0.84` and `avg_free_chunk=384k` vs baseline `avg_free_chunk=1.2M`
matt: can we bisect to the exact commit? suggest `git bisect start HEAD v2026-02-11 && git bisect run ./tests/perf/run_longctx_mem.sh`
ashley: also seeing sequence-length sensitivity: shorter seqs unaffected, spike only at >=2048
sre-ops: I've paused the canary autoscaler to prevent noisy churn while we triage
nora: quick mitigation idea: revert the predictive packing changes and re-run canary, or temporarily tune `slab_min_coalesce` to be more aggressive
zoe: i'll try a local revert-first test and run the repro overnight, will post results in morning
ci-bot: bisect job queued: 2857 -> 2840 range, estimated 12 builds
kai: even if revert helps, we should add regression unit (seq=4096 mem smoke) to CI to catch this class earlier
james: agreed, adding a perf gate for fragmentation metrics makes sense
devx: note: predictive packing increased fill factor, but we didn't account for micro-allocation patterns at payload boundaries — likely root cause
matt: if Zoe confirms fast repro on revert, i'll open rollback PR and coordinate with release to unpause
zoe: repro on revert looks promising locally (no OOM after 30m, frag ratio down to 0.46). pushing samples to perf infra now
sre-ops: thanks — keeping rollout blocked until we have a safe plan. tagging oncall and sig-runtime
ashley: added a short-term slab tuning patch (config) to canary-3 to reduce fragmentation, will monitor metric: `kv_free_compact_rate`
nora: thermal note: these nodes show no GPU pressure, purely allocator + batching interaction
zoe: follow-ups: (1) bisect result, (2) rollback PR if bisect confirms, (3) CI perf test for seq>=2048 frag regression, (4) longer-term: change predictive packing to respect slab coalescing hints
matt: ack. i'll draft rollback and schedule a quick deploy if bisect is conclusive
ci-bot: bisect finished: culprit commit 2857 (predictive packing) confirmed by automated perf run
zoe: thanks. i'll proceed with rollback PR and assign reviewers
devx: logging idea: emit `batch_tail_alloc_size` histogram to help surface this earlier
zoe: good call — adding to follow-up ticket
sre-ops: placing this thread in incident watch until rollout unblocks
zoe: closing loop: rollback PR opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2861, change flagged for canary revert
zoe: will update when canary shows stability or we have rollback deploy time
